classification.difficultyReason: Recognise standard Pascal properties, respect zero-based rows, and test the universal even-entry claim using row 1.

questions.methodNote: Read zero-indexed Pascal rows and use their connection to binomial coefficients.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Recognise elementary properties of Pascal’s triangle and identify a counterexample.

classification.difficultyReason: Adapt a supplied fourth-power expansion by changing the signs of the odd-power terms.

questions.methodNote: Absorb the minus sign into the second term, or alternate signs in the positive expansion.

classification.difficultyReason: Expand conjugate expressions, simplify surd powers, and combine whole expansions while handling subtraction signs correctly.

questions.mappingNote: Preserve the source’s vertical a–b arrangement and shared instruction.
questions.methodNote: Expand the positive and negative binomials separately using Pascal’s row 4, then combine.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply Pascal coefficients to scaled terms, powers of variables and subtraction.

questions.methodNote: Use Pascal’s triangle coefficients, descending and ascending term powers, and negative-term substitution.

classification.difficultyReason: Requires correct alternating signs, surd simplification and a coefficient sum.

questions.mappingNote: Page 3 explicitly demonstrates expanding with a negative second term and explains the resulting alternating signs.
questions.methodNote: Absorb the minus sign into the second binomial term and expand with Pascal coefficients.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Requires correct alternating signs, surd simplification and a coefficient sum.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose rationalisation to rewrite the reciprocal as a binomial, expand its cube, and identify the rational and surd coefficients.

questions.methodNote: Rationalise the reciprocal using prerequisite surd algebra, then expand the cube using Pascal coefficients and a negative second term.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Requires rationalising a reciprocal before applying the cubic Pascal expansion.

classification.difficultyReason: Substitute decimal terms into a fifth-power expansion and evaluate exactly without a calculator.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute decimal terms into a fifth-power expansion and evaluate exactly without a calculator.

classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate a fourth-power numerical expansion exactly, retaining all place values.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine conjugate fifth-power expansions and justify a nearest integer without a calculator.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine conjugate fifth-power expansions and justify a nearest integer without a calculator.

classification.difficultyReason: Connect triangular dot growth with Pascal's recurrence to justify continuation, then interpret the next column as cumulative triangular totals.
